dedupe_keys.name: historic droughts inventory of references from uk agricultural media 1975 2012 cranfield university historic droughts project

description: A qualitative inventory of drought impacts on UK agriculture, drawn from two weekly farming magazines, Farmers Weekly and Farmers Guardian, from 1975 to 2012. The ReShare record says it is the agricultural subset of the UK Drought Inventory built by the Historic Droughts project (2014 to 2018, funded by the UK Research Councils, eight institutions including the British Geological Survey, the Centre for Ecology and Hydrology, the Met Office and Cranfield University), which studied UK drought and water scarcity since the late 19th century. Issues from December 2003 were read electronically and earlier ones in print at the British Library; keywords include crop yields, crop prices, irrigation and livestock. The collection was published on 9 October 2018 and last modified on 27 November 2020 by Dolores Rey, Ian Holman and Jerry Knox; it is open to anyone without registration as a downloadable CSV data file (833 KB) with a supporting information file (4 MB) and a README in RTF, for reference purposes. Coverage is the UK. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 (data file; documentation CC-BY-SA-4.0). For simulation it gives dated accounts of how droughts hit farms, irrigation and prices, to validate drought impact and water allocation models. A related catalogue record is the FAO Agricultural Stress Index System. The underlying files were not downloaded, so their contents are not verified here.
